paper.title: The increase in cell volume and nuclear number of the koji-fungus Aspergillus oryzae contributes to its high enzyme productivity
paper.authors: Itani A, Motomura H, Oda K, Yamashita H, Sakai K, Kusumoto KI, Shigeto S, Ichikawa T, Mubarak HM, Fukuma T, Katayama T, Maruyama JI, Masuo S, Takaya N, Takeshita N.
paper.association_evidence: Methods, data availability: 'The RNA-seq data have been deposited in DDBJ as BioProject PRJDB19992.'

study_summary.objective: Find out why koji-mold hyphae become thick with hundreds of nuclei and whether this increase in cell volume and nuclear number explains the high enzyme secretion of A. oryzae.
study_summary.experimental_design: Colonies of RIB40 and RIB915 grew 3 days at 30 C on minimal-medium agar over cellophane, with or without 1% yeast extract (one library each); thick (3 libraries) and thin (2) hyphae of RIB40 were cut out by laser microdissection.
study_summary.main_finding: Yeast extract made RIB915 form hyphae with more nuclei and raised the expression of 660 genes more than fourfold; thick RIB40 hyphae had 558 such genes and higher ribosome-related expression than thin ones.

cellophane_mm_3d.note: maltose (1%) is the stated MM carbon source in the same paper; not restated for the RNA-seq cultures

notes: The six cellophane-culture libraries (RIB40, RIB915, A. nidulans, each with and without yeast extract) have no biological replicates; only the RIB40 and RIB915 ones are in the atlas.

Cellophane-culture libraries were sequenced as 36 bp paired-end reads on NextSeq 500, microdissected ones as 150 bp paired-end reads on NovaSeq 6000, so the two groups differ in platform and read length as well as in sample type.
The paper describes the RNA-seq medium only as 'minimal medium'; maltose is the carbon source it states for MM in its secretion assays.
